item.title: Star Wars' New Jedi Order Era is Officially Moving Forward
item.dc:creator: Elijah Gonzalez
item.description: [Filtered: Star Wars casting/production gossip falls under big-franchise churn.] Two upcoming Star Wars films, New Jedi Order and Lucasfilm head Dave Filoni's untitled project, are making progress.
item.content:encoded: Despite Star Wars: The Mandalorian & Grogu struggling at the box office, it seems Disney is continuing development on two upcoming Star Wars films. item.title: Where to find the giant crab safe code and Crabshack VF5 SMG in GTA 6
item.dc:creator: Josh Broadwell
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] GTA 6's giant crab event takes you through Pelican Valley Outpost and rewards you with the Crabshack VF5 SMG standout weapon.
item.content:encoded: Grand Theft Auto 6has a giant crab haunting the swamps and, more importantly, the Crabshack VF5 SMG, a crab-themed gun, to help your future career prospects. It's all part of an optional event called Pelican Valley Outpost that sees you pick up the pieces of some questionable experiments carried out on behalf of a store chain. It's worth the trouble, even aside from the standout weapon. There's some cash to help reach your next family fund milestone and a free jet ski, too. Best of all, this little excursion is completely safe, assuming you don't run afoul of the local gator population.

item.title: George R.R. Martin’s 7 Best Non-Game of Thrones Books, Ranked
item.dc:creator: Ryan Epps
item.description: [Filtered: Graphic-novel/book promo excerpt; not game-related content.] From antebellum Mississippi vampires to cat-loving space traders, George R.R. Martin’s best work goes far beyond Westeros and Game of Thrones.
item.content:encoded: George R.R. Martin will forever be associated with his book series, A Song of Ice and Fire, and HBO’s adaptation, Game of Thrones, but there's considerably more to his bibliography than scheming Lannisters, fire-breathing dragons, and the unending wait for The Winds of Winter. Long before Westeros became a cultural phenomenon, Martin was building a reputation as one of science fiction and fantasy's most imaginative voices, writing everything from supernatural mysteries and vampiric thrillers to sprawling space operas and intimate character dramas.

item.title: Gary Larson's 10 Greatest 'Far Side' Comics, Ranked
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective of old comic strip; filler content.] Gary Larson's comic strip The Far Side was at its greatest when it was really, really funny. That's why is these are his 10 best comics
item.content:encoded: What, exactly, is the measure of greatness when it comes to comic strips? The daily newspaper comic is a very limiting art form, with only a few panels — sometimes just one panel — to make a joke. Because of its brevity, it's easy to trivialize the medium as simply the “funny papers,” a daily, disposable art form designed to pick you up after reading the actual news.

item.title: 9 Calvin and Hobbes Comics from the 1990s that Prove Bill Watterson is a Genius
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective of classic 1990s comic strip.] Calvin and Hobbes creator Bill Watterson is a genius. Here are nine comics which prove it.
item.content:encoded: Calvin and Hobbescreator Bill Watterson is a genius. Over the course of ten years spanning more than 3,000 comic strips, he developed two truly irresistible characters that are still beloved by millions. There was a lot behind the success of Calvin and Hobbes, but I think part of the reason why Watterson is still so widely respected is that he was an incredibly versatile artist who managed to do a lot of different things in an artform that can sometimes be limiting.

item.title: 44 Years Later, Steven Spielberg's Scariest Movie of All Time Is Officially Free on Streaming
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Horror classic streaming availability clickbait; retroactive content.] The supernatural horror film Poltergeist is on Pluto TV, though there's still a debate as to who directed it
item.content:encoded: Poltergeist, which became available to stream for free on Pluto TV on Nov. 1, follows an ordinary suburban family that begins to experience strange things in their home. Furniture and toys move on their own, a glass of milk shatters out of nowhere, and the youngest child in the family, 5-year-old Carol Anne (Heather O'Rourke), begins to communicate with beings through the television. At first, these events are dismissed, but during a thunderstorm one night, a tree outside the windows of the kids’ room crashes in and snatches the boy. Then, a portal opens in their closet, sucking Carol Anne into another dimension. With help from some paranormal investigators, the family tries everything to bring her back.

item.title: 53 Years Later, The Greatest Closing Line In Sci-Fi History Is Still The Best Book Quote Of The 1970s
item.dc:creator: Ryan Epps
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about old book; not game/horror/prestige film.] Roadside Picnic ends with one of science fiction’s most beautiful lines, a simple wish for happiness that still resonates more than 50 years later.
item.content:encoded: The canon of science-fiction literature is home to countless unforgettable endings, from 1984’s short but devastating retrospective ("He loved Big Brother") to The Three-Body Problem’s defiant reminder that humanity cannot be so easily wiped out. The best sci-fi endings don't offer comfortable closure. Instead, they reframe everything that came before. In their closing lines, great sci-fi novelists leave readers suspended in the aftermath, forced to stew in the terrifying logic of cold technology, the fragility of human nature, and the vast expanse of space.

item.title: 10 Funniest 'Far Side' Comics About Cavemen and Their Early Innovations

item.content:encoded: Gary Larson’s comic strip The Far Side broke the mold of traditional newspaper comics by not having a recurring cast of characters. Peanuts had Charlie Brown, Snoopy, Linus and the rest of the gang. Garfield had Garfield, Odie, Jon, and some others. Calvin and Hobbes had Calvin, Hobbes, and Calvin’s parents. But The Far Side introduced new characters and scenarios every single day.

item.title: 'Calvin and Hobbes' Best Miss Wormwood Quote Is Still Among the Smartest in Comic Strip History
item.dc:creator: Thomas Hindmarch
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about old comic strip, not a game.] Looking back at Miss Wormwood's best moments in Calvin and Hobbes
item.content:encoded: Bill Watterson walked a few different tightropes when he created Calvin and Hobbes, one of which involved Calvin's relationship with school. It would've been easy to make it simply antagonistic, with Calvin as the hero fighting back against the dark forces of educational conformity, a bit like a comic adaptation of Pink Floyd's "Another Brick in the Wall." Any number of later webcomics that were unsubtly inspired by Calvin and Hobbes went this way, at least at first.

item.title: 8 Funniest 'Far Side' Comics Starring Cowboys
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about old comic strip, not gaming/core content.] Gary Larson’s comic strip The Far Side loved to parody cowboys in the Old West. Here are the eight best
item.content:encoded: Gary Larson, the comedy genius behind The Far Sidecomic strip, loved to turn things into their opposites. Serious, brilliant scientists were cast as childish dummies who drop everything when they hear an ice cream truck pass by. Simple-minded cows could be so smart that they plot the deaths of their owners. As for cowboys, the manly men of the Old West, Larson loved to portray them as meek and cowardly.

item.title: 10 Sci-Fi Books You Need to Read Before At Least Once In Your Life
item.dc:creator: Jake Kleinman
item.description: [Filtered: Generic book list, not video game or prestige film/TV coverage.] The ultimate reading list for mind-bending, genre-defining speculative fiction
item.content:encoded: Science fiction remains one of storytelling's most expansive playgrounds, capable of charting distant space just as easily as it exposes the imminent horrors of near-future technology. At its peak, sci-fi uses invented technology and distant planets to interrogate what it means to be human, cracking open eternal philosophical questions that more grounded genres simply can’t.

item.title: 66 Years Later, William Shatner's Forgotten 'Twilight Zone' Is Still a Haunting Masterpiece
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective; old episode isn't new prestige/anticipated project.] The Twilight Zone episode “Nick of Time” is top-tier Shatner
item.content:encoded: “Nightmare at 20,000 Feet” is one of the all-time great episodes of The Twilight Zone. Starring William Shatner, the story is about a man who is taking his first flight after having had a nervous breakdown. During the flight, he looks out the window and sees a creature, called a gremlin, on the wing that taunts him and tears apart pieces of the plane. No one can see the gremlin but him, and even his own wife attributes it to his fragile mental state. The story is a brilliant commentary on paranoia and Shatner was captivating in the role. It was so good that it sometimes overshadows Shatner’s other great episode of The Twilight Zone, which premiered 66 years ago today.

item.title: 63 Years Later, the Best 'Peanuts' Sally Line Is Still an Iconic Comic Strip Quote
item.dc:creator: Thomas Hindmarch
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about decades-old comic strip.] In Peanuts, it's Sally Brown vs. school
item.content:encoded: Charlie Brown might be the unluckiest character in the Western canon. The degree to which the universe conspires to dump misfortune directly on his head over and over is the beating heart of Charles Schulz's Peanuts. If you've got any problems at all, you can check in on good ol' Charlie Brown and be slightly cheered up by the knowledge that at least you've got it better than him.

item.title: New 'Pokémon' TCG Lucario Set Leaks In Stores Months Before Official Release
item.dc:creator: Patricia Hernandez
item.description: [Filtered: Pokémon TCG retail/restock story, matches toss pattern.] Flowing Fists, the next Pokémon set after Delta Reign, isn't scheduled until 2027 yet people are already pulling its chase card
item.content:encoded: The Pokémon Trading Card Game's latest set, Delta Reign, just came out a couple of weeks ago in early November. The next set, Flowing Fists, isn't scheduled to drop for another few months. Most people haven't seen Delta Reign boxes in stores yet, never mind the recent Pokémon 30th Anniversary set. Despite all of this, real people have apparently already acquired packs of Flowing Fist. Heck, some people have already pulled the next set's chase card — which hasn't even been formally revealed yet!

item.title: All active Aniimo codes list
item.dc:creator: Josh Broadwell
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] Aniimo codes get you free Glimmer to spend in the in-game shop and some helpful level-up mats, too. These are all the active Aniimo codes
item.content:encoded: Aniimo codes give you bonus level-up materials and other currency, including glimmer. It might not have a traditional gacha system, but these freebies come in handy anyway. For one thing, you need a lot of level-up materials once you start raising your aniimo army. Plus you can use Glimmer in the in-game shop to buy useful items or the currency you can exchange for Sparkling Cubes to use on eggs. If none of that takes your fancy, you can always just keep it for later, too.
